question: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE) Subject:

On 13 April 2026, the Joint Congress-Senate Committee on the European Union of the Spanish Cortes Generales adopted a resolution urging the Government to reject the EU-UK Agreement in respect of Gibraltar1. The Cortes Generales, which, pursuant to the Constitution, have the power to give or withhold approval for the conclusion of international treaties that are binding upon the State, have rejected the Agreement on the grounds that it runs counter to the Spanish claim of sovereignty over the British colony, which is afforded a much more favourable regime than it enjoyed during the United Kingdom’s membership of the European Union, and indeed than that stipulated under the Treaty of Utrecht. It also condemned the Agreement for failing to equalise taxation between the Gibraltar and Campo de Gibraltar. The Cortes Generales also rejected the Agreement on the grounds that the Government is in breach of the Constitution by not submitting it for prior approval. In light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission still intend to ratify a treaty which has not been approved by the Parliament of the Member State concerned and which holds the title of sovereignty over Gibraltar?
Does it consider that the mere approval by the European Parliament dispenses with the obligation to seek the approval of the national parliament of the State concerned?
https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CORT/BOCG/A/BOCG-15-CG-A-230.PDF#page=2
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.8.2026) 1. The EU-United Kingdom Agreement in respect of Gibraltar represents the last element that completes the legal framework of the relations between the EU and the United Kingdom following Brexit. The legal basis for the conclusion of the EU-United Kingdom Agreement in respect of Gibraltar is Article 217 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)1, according to which the EU has competence to conclude association agreements with third countries. The procedure for the conclusion of association agreements is foreseen in Article 218 TFEU2. On this basis, the Council takes the decision authorising the signature of the agreement and its provisional application and it is also for the Council to conclude the agreement, after obtaining the consent of the European Parliament. These decisions are adopted by the Council by unanimity. The same procedure was used for the conclusion of the EU-United Kingdom Trade and Cooperation Agreement3. 2. The EU-United Kingdom Agreement in respect of Gibraltar states that it shall be without prejudice to legal positions of Spain and the United Kingdom with regard to sovereignty and jurisdiction and shall not constitute the basis for any assertion or denial of sovereignty including in legal proceedings or otherwise.
